tasks.short: Set objectives and outline, draft lesson plans and handouts, select and write exam items, check with a subject teacher and publish.

steps.what: Coordinator sets learning objectives and the outline for the unit
Coordinator develops lesson plans and handouts

loop.input: The unit outline with learning objectives and the approved source texts for the unit.
loop.output: Draft lesson plans and handouts per lesson, each activity tagged with the objective it serves.
loop.check: Code checks every objective is covered by at least one activity and every fact box cites a source text; the coordinator edits every draft before use.
loop.stop: One draft per lesson; on failure the coordinator writes the lesson.
loop.why_not_simpler: Lesson plans are free text built around objectives; templates give structure but not content.

steps.what: Coordinator selects and writes examination items with answer keys
Coordinator checks the materials with a subject teacher and finalises them
Coordinator uploads the unit materials to the course pages

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts lesson plans and handouts from the unit outline and approved source texts, and code checks objective coverage and source citations; the coordinator edits every draft. Exam items come from an item bank searchable by objective, with new items written by hand. After the subject teacher check, the unit is published to the learning platform ({LMS}). Exams are never published to learners before the test date.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lessons, handouts and items were written from scratch for each unit.
tasks.enabler_now: A trial found AI lesson assistance cut preparation time; item banks tag items by objective.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can be plausible but wrong; exam items need careful checking.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which example will make the idea click for this group.
tasks.altitude: The coordinator edits drafted lessons instead of writing them.

reach.learn: Whether teachers adopt drafted lesson plans.

evidence.claim: In a randomised trial in England, teachers using an AI lesson assistant spent 49 minutes less a week on lesson preparation, with quality no worse.
Snappet generates a classroom activity from the lesson's learning objective.
Schools must keep personal data out of AI tools, sign a processor agreement and do a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from objectives to published materials; teaching is outside.
Input contract: curriculum set by the curriculum team; approved source texts chosen by the coordinator; item bank kept by the exam team; fallback is writing by hand.
Objectives and the teacher check stay with people.
Teacher time is outside the coordinator's savings.
research_questions: How much of each draft survives editing?

incremental.description: Coordinator tags new items by objective in the bank.

approvals.approved_version: The unit materials as finalised by the coordinator in s4; later edits need a new check before publishing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the accreditation requirements, draft manual sections from course files, check coverage, format to the template, get approval, submit and answer questions.

steps.what: Coordinator reads the accreditation requirements and maps them to the course
Coordinator develops master course documentation from the existing course files

loop.input: The requirement map and the course's existing files: course plan, objectives, assessment plan and materials.
loop.output: Draft manual sections per requirement, each sentence linked to the course file it comes from.
loop.check: Code checks every sentence links to a course file and every requirement has a section; the coordinator edits every section.
loop.stop: One draft per section; sections without source files stay empty for the coordinator.
loop.why_not_simpler: Course files differ in structure; copying them into a template does not answer the requirements.

steps.what: Coordinator checks every requirement is covered with evidence
Coordinator formats the manual to the accreditor's template
Programme manager reviews and approves the manual
Coordinator uploads the manual to the accreditor's portal
Coordinator answers the accreditor's follow-up questions

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts manual sections per accreditation requirement from the course's own files, linking every sentence to its source; code flags requirements without a section or evidence, and the document system ({DOCS}) applies the accreditor's template. The programme manager approves the manual; only then is it submitted through the accreditor's portal. Mapping requirements and answering the accreditor stay with the coordinator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manuals were assembled by copying from many course files into a template by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Course authoring tools draft documentation from existing files, and coverage checks are plain code.
tasks.still_hard: Accreditors judge substance; a complete document can still describe a weak course.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining to a panel why the course is built the way it is.
tasks.altitude: The coordinator edits linked drafts instead of copying files together.

reach.learn: Whether linked drafts cut preparation time.

evidence.claim: Easygenerator drafts a course from PowerPoint or PDF; vendor claims up to nine times faster.
Accreditors judge programmes on the submitted file; the institution is responsible for its accuracy.

assumptions: Boundary: from requirements to answered questions; the accreditation decision is outside.
Input contract: requirements published by the accreditor; course files kept by the course teams; template from the accreditor; fallback is copying by hand.
Programme manager time is outside the coordinator's savings.
No student data go into the drafting step.

incremental.description: Coordinator keeps course files in the expected folders.

approvals.approved_version: The manual as approved by the programme manager in s5; any change needs a new approval before submission.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Courses with scattered files gain less.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define what to measure, select items, build the survey or test, pilot it and check reliability, and revise items.

steps.what: Coordinator defines what to measure with stakeholders
Coordinator writes survey and test items for the measurement tools
Coordinator builds the survey or test in the survey tool
Coordinator pilots the tool and computes reliability statistics in a spreadsheet
Coordinator revises items after the pilot

tasks.design: An item bank of tried survey and test items, tagged by what they measure, lets the coordinator pick items instead of writing them all, and the survey tool ({OTHER}) imports the chosen set. After the pilot, the tool computes reliability and item statistics automatically for the coordinator to interpret. Defining what to measure and revising items stay with the coordinator; no AI writes or scores items.
tasks.previous_blocker: Items were written from scratch and statistics computed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Survey tools import items from banks and compute reliability statistics.
tasks.still_hard: Valid measurement needs judgement about what an item really measures.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a question measures reading skill, not the training's effect.
tasks.altitude: The coordinator selects and interprets instead of writing and computing.

reach.learn: Whether a shared item bank makes evaluations comparable.

evidence.claim: Survey tools import items from banks and compute reliability statistics.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk; this design uses no AI.

assumptions: Boundary: from goals to the revised tool; running the evaluation is outside.
Input contract: training goals from the stakeholders; item bank kept by the coordinator; fallback is writing items.
Defining and revising stay with the coordinator.
Pilot respondents' time is outside the savings.
research_questions: Do bank items give more reliable scales?

incremental.description: Coordinator adds tested items to the bank.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read drafts and mark content issues, correct language and style, check references and numbering, discuss changes with authors and track versions.

steps.what: Coordinator reads draft instructional materials and marks content issues
Coordinator corrects language, style and consistency

loop.input: The draft text and the house style guide.
loop.output: Suggested edits as tracked changes, each naming the style rule it applies.
loop.check: Code checks every suggestion stays within one sentence, names a style rule and leaves numbers, terms and test answers unchanged; the coordinator accepts or rejects each suggestion.
loop.stop: One pass per chapter; no second pass on accepted text.
loop.why_not_simpler: Clarity and tone rules cannot be written as spelling or pattern checks.

steps.what: Coordinator checks references, figure numbers and cross-references
Coordinator discusses changes with the authors
Coordinator tracks versions by renaming files

tasks.design: A bounded step suggests style edits as tracked changes against the house style guide, never touching numbers, terms or test answers, and the coordinator accepts or rejects each. Code checks references, figure numbers and cross-references, and the document system ({DOCS}) keeps versions. Reading for content and agreeing changes with authors stay with the coordinator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Style, numbering and versions were checked and managed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models can suggest style edits against a guide; reference checks are plain code.
tasks.still_hard: A smooth sentence can carry a wrong fact; content editing stays human.
tasks.human_edge: Telling an author kindly that a chapter does not work.
tasks.altitude: The coordinator judges suggested edits instead of making every one.

reach.learn: Whether style suggestions shorten editing rounds.

evidence.claim: LessonUp rewrites slide text by tone or level.
Schools must keep personal data out of AI tools, sign a processor agreement and do a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from author drafts to versioned agreed text; printing is outside.
Input contract: drafts from authors; house style guide kept by the coordinator; fallback is editing by hand.
Content reading and author talks do not change.
Authors' time is outside the coordinator's savings.
research_questions: What share of suggested edits is accepted?

already_counted.description: Coordinator accepts or rejects each suggestion.

incremental.description: Coordinator keeps the style guide in a form the checks can use.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Materials needing heavy content edits save less.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The instructional coordinator keeps objectives, content judgement and work with teachers and authors; first drafts, formatting and statistics shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A coordinator who produces better materials faster by editing rather than writing from scratch.
